33829.e: A helmet only protects you well if it fits your head size. That is why you try it on before buying it.
33829.m: You try on a bike helmet before buying it.

33830.q: Which Swiss organisation works to prevent accidents and recommends bike helmets?
33830.e: The BFU is the Swiss Council for Accident Prevention. It gives tips on how to avoid accidents.
33830.m: The BFU helps to prevent accidents.

33831.q: What colour is a zebra crossing in Switzerland?
33831.e: In Switzerland, zebra crossings are marked in yellow. In many other countries they are white.
33831.m: In Switzerland, zebra crossings are yellow.

33832.q: Why is the pedestrian crossing called a zebra crossing?
a: It has stripes like a zebra
It was invented at the zoo
It is black like the night
33832.e: The wide stripes remind people of a zebra's coat. That is why it is called a zebra crossing.
33832.m: A zebra crossing has stripes like a zebra.

33833.q: Where is the safest place for you to cross a road?
33833.e: At a zebra crossing, drivers expect pedestrians and must stop. Between cars or on bends, you can easily be overlooked.
33833.m: It is best to cross the road at the zebra crossing.

33834.q: At a zebra crossing without traffic lights, who has priority over cars?
33834.e: Cars must stop before the zebra crossing when someone wants to cross the road. Pedestrians have priority there.
33834.m: At a zebra crossing, pedestrians have priority over cars.

33835.q: Which vehicle has priority over pedestrians in Switzerland, even at a zebra crossing?
33835.e: A tram cannot swerve and only brakes slowly. That is why it has priority even at a zebra crossing.
33835.m: You must wait for a tram, even at a zebra crossing.

33836.q: When do you cross at a zebra crossing if a car is coming?
a: As soon as the car indicates
33836.e: The Swiss rule is “wheel stops, child goes”. Only when the car has stopped completely is it safe.

33837.q: How do you cross the zebra crossing?
a: Stand in the middle of the road
33837.e: If you run, you can trip or be overlooked. That is why you walk briskly and watch the traffic.
33837.m: You cross the zebra crossing briskly, but you don't run.

33838.q: What is the safe place in the middle of a wide road called, where pedestrians can wait?
33838.e: Wide roads often have a traffic island. There you can wait and only have to watch one lane at a time.
33838.m: You can wait safely on the traffic island.

33839.q: What is a lost property office?
33839.e: Found items are kept at the lost property office. If you have lost something, you can ask there.
33839.m: At the lost property office, you can find lost things again.

33840.q: What do you do with a purse that you find in the street?
a: Take it to the lost property office
Leave it there and walk away
33840.e: Things you find belong to someone else. You take them to the lost property office or to the police.
33840.m: You take things you find to the lost property office.

33841.q: Where is the lost property office often found in Switzerland?
33841.e: In Switzerland, the municipalities or the police usually run a lost property office. You report found items there.
33841.m: The lost property office is often at the municipality.

33842.q: Where do things go that have been left behind on a train?
a: To the railway's lost property office
33842.e: The railway collects forgotten things and takes them to its lost property office. You can collect them from there.
33842.m: Things forgotten on the train end up at the railway's lost property office.

33843.q: What can the finder ask the owner for?
33843.e: Anyone who returns something that was lost may ask for a reasonable finder's reward. This is set out in the law.
33843.m: Honest finders may ask for a finder's reward.

33844.q: After how many years does a reported found item belong to the finder if nobody comes forward?
33844.e: If you report a find properly and the owner has not been found after five years, you become the owner of the item.
33844.m: After five years, a reported found item belongs to the finder.

33845.q: May you simply keep things you have found?
33845.e: Anyone who simply keeps a found item commits an offence. You must report or hand in what you find.
33845.m: You may not simply keep things you have found.

33846.q: What is best to write in your school things so that they can be returned to you?
33846.e: If your name is on something, the finder or the lost property office knows who it belongs to.
33846.m: With your name on it, a lost item finds its way back more easily.

33847.q: What is in a law book?
33847.e: A law book collects the laws on a topic. That way you can look up the rules.
33847.m: Laws are collected in a law book.

33848.q: What is the Swiss code called that says which acts are crimes?
33848.e: The Criminal Code states which acts are forbidden and what punishments they can bring. Its abbreviation in German is StGB.
33848.m: The Criminal Code lists forbidden acts and their punishments.

33850.q: Roughly how old is the Swiss Civil Code (as of 2025)?
33850.e: The Civil Code has been in force since 1912. But it has been changed many times since then.
33850.m: The Civil Code is over a hundred years old.

33851.q: What are the numbered sections in a law called?
33851.e: Laws are divided into numbered articles. That way you can find a rule exactly, for example Article 1.
33851.m: A law is divided into numbered articles.

33852.q: In which three official languages are federal laws published with equal status?
33852.e: Federal laws are equally valid in German, French and Italian. Important texts are also available in Romansh.
33852.m: Federal laws are published in German, French and Italian.

33853.q: Where can anyone in Switzerland read all federal laws for free?
33853.e: The federal laws are published free of charge on the internet on the Fedlex platform. That way anyone can look them up.
33853.m: You can read all federal laws for free on the internet.

33854.q: Which law governs traffic on the roads in Switzerland?
33854.e: The Road Traffic Act contains the rules for cars, bikes and pedestrians. Its abbreviation in German is SVG.
33854.m: The Road Traffic Act governs traffic.

33855.q: Which Swiss law governs purchase contracts and rental agreements?
33855.e: The Code of Obligations (OR in German) governs contracts such as buying, renting and employment.
33855.m: The Code of Obligations governs contracts such as buying and renting.

33856.q: Where do you take empty glass bottles in your municipality?
33856.e: Empty glass bottles belong at the glass collection point. There the glass is collected and made into new glass.
33856.m: I take old glass to the glass collection point.

33857.q: Which colours is old glass sorted into at the collection point?
33857.e: Glass is sorted into clear, brown and green. That way it can be made into glass of the same colour again.
33857.m: Old glass is sorted into clear, brown and green.

33858.e: In recycling, collected material such as paper, glass or PET is made into new things. That means fewer new raw materials are needed.
33858.m: In recycling, something new is made from waste.

33859.q: How do you tie up waste paper for the paper collection?
a: With tape all the way round
33859.e: Waste paper is bundled and tied together with string. That way it can be collected easily and doesn't blow away.
33859.m: I tie up waste paper with string.

33860.q: Where do vegetable peelings such as carrot peel go?
33860.e: Peelings from vegetables and fruit go into the green waste or on the compost. New soil is made from them.
33860.m: Vegetable peelings go in the green waste or on the compost.

33861.q: Where do you take used batteries?
33861.e: Batteries contain harmful substances. You take them back to a shop that sells them, where there are collection boxes.
33861.m: I take used batteries back to the shop.

a: Taking rubbish to the collection point
33862.e: Littering means that someone simply throws rubbish on the ground or into nature. It is bad for animals and the environment and can be fined.
33862.m: Rubbish belongs in the bin, not on the ground.

33863.q: Where can you hand in bulky waste such as an old sofa in many municipalities?
a: At the municipal depot or recycling centre
33863.e: Large items of rubbish are called bulky waste. Many municipalities accept bulky waste at the recycling centre or on special collection days.
33863.m: Bulky waste goes to the recycling centre or on the collection day.

33864.q: When should you not put glass into the glass collection point?
33864.e: Throwing glass in makes a lot of noise. That is why many municipalities don't allow it on Sundays and at night.
33864.m: You don't throw glass in on Sundays or at night.

33865.q: What goes into the rubbish bag?
33865.e: Only waste that cannot be reused goes into the rubbish bag. Glass, paper and batteries are collected separately.
33865.m: Only waste that can't be sorted goes into the rubbish bag.

33866.q: Why does an official rubbish bag cost money in many municipalities?
a: It pays for the rubbish collection
Because it is made of fabric
33866.e: The bag charge pays for collecting and burning the rubbish. People who produce more rubbish pay more.
33866.m: If you produce more rubbish, you pay more with the bag charge.

33867.q: What is a rubbish fee sticker?
a: A sticker for the rubbish bag
An entrance ticket for the cinema
33867.e: In some municipalities, you stick a fee sticker on the rubbish bag. That shows the disposal has been paid for.
33867.m: A fee sticker shows that the rubbish has been paid for.

33868.q: Who collects the rubbish bags from the street?
33868.e: The bin collectors drive a dustcart through the municipality. They collect the bags on collection day.
33868.m: The bin collectors take the rubbish away on collection day.

33869.q: When do you put the rubbish bag out on the street?
33869.e: You only put the rubbish bag out on collection day. Otherwise animals such as foxes or crows can tear the bag open.
33869.m: I only put the rubbish bag out on collection day.

33870.q: Where does the dustcart usually take the rubbish?
33870.e: In Switzerland, rubbish is burnt in a waste incineration plant. The fumes are carefully cleaned there.
33870.m: Rubbish is burnt in a waste incineration plant.

33871.q: What can a waste incineration plant make from the heat of the fire?
33871.e: Burning rubbish produces a lot of heat. The plant uses it to produce electricity and heat for warming homes.
33871.m: Electricity and heat are gained from burnt rubbish.

33872.q: What is the official fee-paid rubbish bag in the city of Zurich called?
33872.e: In the city of Zurich, the official fee-paid rubbish bag is called the “Züri-Sack”. Other municipalities have their own bags with their own names.
33872.m: Many municipalities have their own official rubbish bag.

33873.q: What may you not burn yourself in the garden?
33873.e: Burning rubbish in the garden is forbidden in Switzerland. It produces poisonous gases that harm people and nature.
33873.m: You never burn rubbish yourself in the garden.

33874.q: Where does most of our drinking water in Switzerland come from?
33874.e: About 80 percent of drinking water in Switzerland comes from spring water and groundwater. The rest comes mainly from lakes.
33874.m: Our drinking water mostly comes from springs and groundwater.

33875.q: Can you drink water from the tap in Switzerland?
33875.e: Tap water in Switzerland is drinking water. It is checked regularly.
33875.m: In Switzerland, you can drink tap water.

33877.q: Where is drinking water often stored before it flows into houses?
a: In the fountain on the village square
33877.e: A reservoir is a large water store, often on a hill. From there the water flows through pipes into the houses.
33877.m: Drinking water is stored in a reservoir.

33878.q: How does drinking water get into houses?
33878.e: Drinking water flows through mains, that is pipes under the ground. That way it reaches every tap.
33878.m: Drinking water flows through pipes into our houses.

33879.q: Where does the dirty water from the washbasin go?
33879.e: Waste water flows through the sewers to the sewage treatment plant. There it is cleaned before it goes back into a river or lake.
33879.m: Dirty water is cleaned at the sewage treatment plant.

33880.q: What are the pipes under the road for waste water called?
33880.e: The sewers are a network of pipes under the ground. They carry waste water to the sewage treatment plant.
33880.m: The sewers carry waste water to the treatment plant.

33881.q: What does the water meter in a house show?
a: How much water has been used
33881.e: The water meter measures how much water a house uses. The municipality uses it to work out how much you have to pay.
33881.m: The water meter measures how much water we use.

33882.q: What is a hydrant on the street?
a: A water connection for the fire brigade
33882.e: A hydrant is connected to the water mains. The fire brigade attaches its hoses there to put out a fire.
33882.m: The fire brigade gets water for fighting fires from the hydrant.

33883.q: Who is usually responsible for primary school in Switzerland?
33883.e: The municipalities run the primary schools. The canton sets many of the rules, for example the curriculum.
33883.m: The municipality runs the primary school in the village.

33884.q: How many years does primary school last in most cantons?
33884.e: In most cantons, primary school lasts six years, from Year 1 to Year 6. After that comes lower secondary school.
33884.m: Primary school usually lasts six years.

33885.q: What comes before primary school in Switzerland?
33885.e: Before primary school, children go to kindergarten. In most cantons it lasts two years.
33885.m: Before primary school, children go to kindergarten.

33886.q: Do you have to pay school fees for state primary school?
33886.e: Lessons at state schools in Switzerland are free of charge. This is written in the Federal Constitution.
33886.m: State primary school costs no school fees.

33887.q: What is the building where school takes place called?
33887.e: The building where school takes place is called the school building. It often also has a gym and a playground.
33887.m: School takes place in the school building.

33888.q: Who makes sure that everything in the school building is clean and in order?
33888.e: The caretaker looks after the school building. They repair small things and make sure it is clean.
33888.m: The caretaker looks after the school building.

33889.q: What is the group called that runs and supervises the school in a municipality?
33889.e: The school board or school committee is a municipal authority. It supervises the school together with the school management.
33889.m: The school board supervises the municipality's school.

33890.q: Where can some children eat at lunchtime if nobody is at home?
33890.e: Many municipalities offer a lunch club. There children eat together, looked after by adults.
33890.m: At the lunch club, children eat together at midday.

33891.q: What is a school crossing patrol?
a: A helper for crossing the road
33891.e: School crossing patrols help children cross the road safely on their way to school. They wear bright vests so that they can be seen easily.
33891.m: School crossing patrols help children cross the road safely.

33892.q: Who often builds and looks after public playgrounds?
33892.e: Public playgrounds often belong to the municipality. Its staff check and repair the play equipment.
33892.m: The municipality builds and looks after public playgrounds.

33893.q: What is a climbing spider at the playground?
a: A climbing frame made of ropes
A real animal in the sand
33893.e: A climbing spider is a net of strong ropes. It looks like a spider's web, and children can climb in it.
33893.m: In the climbing spider, you climb in a net of ropes.

33894.q: What do you do if a piece of play equipment at the playground is broken?
33894.e: Broken play equipment can be dangerous. You report it to the municipality so that it gets repaired.
33894.m: I report broken play equipment to the municipality.

33895.q: Why is a sandpit often covered?
a: So that animals don't use it as a toilet
So that the sand gets warm
So that the sand stays wet
33895.e: Cats and other animals like to use open sandpits as a toilet. A cover keeps the sand clean.
33895.m: A cover keeps the sandpit clean.

33896.q: What is not allowed in many playgrounds?
33896.e: In many playgrounds, dogs are not allowed or must be on a lead. That keeps the area clean and safe for children.
33896.m: Dogs are not allowed in many playgrounds.

33897.q: What can you do at a water playground?
33897.e: A water playground has pumps, channels and little sluices. Children can play with the water there and change its course.
33897.m: At the water playground, children play with water.

33898.q: Who is a public playground for?
33898.e: A public playground is there for everyone. Nobody has to pay to get in.
33898.m: A public playground is open to all children.

a: A playground for building and making things
A playground in the indoor pool
33899.e: At an adventure playground, children may build with wood, make things and light fires. Adults supervise them.
33899.m: At an adventure playground, children may build things themselves.

33900.q: What can you borrow from a public library?
33900.e: At the library you can borrow books and bring them back later. There are often audiobooks, films and games too.
33900.m: I borrow books from the library.

33901.q: What do you usually need to borrow books?
33901.e: With the library card, the library knows who has borrowed which book. For children it is often free.
33901.m: With a library card, I can borrow books.

33902.q: What happens if you bring a book back late?
a: You have to keep the book
33902.e: At many libraries, there is a small late fee if you are late. That way the books come back on time.
33902.m: I bring borrowed books back on time.

33903.q: How do you behave in a library?
33903.e: Many people read and study in a library. That is why you are quiet and considerate there.
33903.m: In the library, I am quiet.

33904.q: Who helps you find a suitable book in the library?
33904.e: Librarians know the books well. They help with searching and borrowing.
33904.m: The librarian helps me find a book.

33905.q: How are the books in a library arranged?
a: By topic and in alphabetical order
By the colour of the cover
33905.e: Books are arranged by topic and often alphabetically by the author's name. That way you can find them quickly.
33905.m: In the library, the books are well organised.

33906.q: What is a story time at the library?
a: Someone reads stories aloud to children
You have to sit a test
33906.e: At story time, someone reads exciting stories aloud to the children. Many libraries offer this.
33906.m: At story time, children listen to stories.

33907.q: Where do you return a book when the library is closed?
a: On the ground outside the door
33907.e: Many libraries have a returns box. You can drop books into it even when the library is closed.
33907.m: If the library is closed, I use the returns box.

33908.q: Which emergency number do you call in Switzerland if there is a fire?
33908.e: The emergency number for the fire brigade is 118. 117 is for the police and 144 for the ambulance.
33908.m: If there is a fire, I call 118.

33909.q: What colour are fire engines in Switzerland usually?
33909.e: Fire engines are usually red. That way they can be seen easily.

33910.q: Where are the fire brigade's vehicles kept when they are not on a call-out?
33910.e: The fire brigade's vehicles and equipment are kept at the fire station. They set off from there to emergencies.
33910.m: Fire engines wait at the fire station for a call-out.

33911.q: What else do most firefighters in Swiss villages have?
a: A flat in the fire station
33911.e: Most firefighters in Switzerland have another job. When there is a fire, they help in their municipality's fire brigade.
33911.m: Most firefighters also have another job.

33912.q: What else does the fire brigade do apart from putting out fires?
33912.e: The fire brigade also helps in storms, floods and accidents. It rescues people and animals.
33912.m: The fire brigade helps in many emergencies.

33913.q: How does a fire engine warn people on the way to an emergency?
a: With blue lights and a siren
33913.e: Blue lights and a siren show everyone that there is an emergency. Other vehicles then make room.
33913.m: When I see blue lights and hear a siren, I make room straight away.

33914.q: What should you do if there is a fire in your flat?
33914.e: In a fire, you get out straight away and then call the fire brigade. You do not use the lift, and hiding is dangerous.
33914.m: If there is a fire, I get out straight away.

33915.q: What gives an early warning of smoke in a flat?
33915.e: A smoke alarm beeps loudly when it detects smoke. That way you can get to safety early.
33915.m: A smoke alarm warns loudly of smoke.

33916.q: Which machine cleans roads and pavements?
33916.e: The road sweeper has rotating brushes. It picks up dust, leaves and rubbish from the road.
33916.m: The road sweeper cleans roads with brushes.

33917.q: What is the green Robidog bin for?
33917.e: At the Robidog there are little bags for dog poo. Dog owners pick up the poo with them and throw it into the bin.
33917.m: Dog poo goes into the Robidog.

33918.q: Who is responsible for cleaning the public roads in a municipality?
33918.e: Staff from the works department or municipal depot keep the roads clean. They also empty the litter bins.
33918.m: The municipal works department keeps the roads clean.

33919.q: What does the municipality sweep off the roads a lot in autumn?
33919.e: In autumn, lots of leaves fall from the trees. Wet leaves can be slippery, so they are cleared away.
33919.m: In autumn, the municipality clears away lots of leaves.

33920.q: Why is it good when everyone throws their rubbish in the bin?
a: The road sweeper has more work
33920.e: If nobody throws rubbish on the ground, the municipality stays clean. That also saves work and money on cleaning.
33920.m: Disposing of rubbish properly keeps the municipality clean.

33921.q: When is there often a lot of cleaning to do after a village festival?
33921.e: After a festival, there is a lot of rubbish lying around. The municipality or the helpers usually clean up the very next day.
33921.m: After a festival, things are tidied up quickly.

33922.e: On Clean-Up Day, lots of people volunteer to collect litter in nature and in their municipality. School classes join in too.
33922.m: On Clean-Up Day, lots of people collect litter together.

33923.q: Who empties the public litter bins at the bus stop?
33923.e: The litter bins are emptied by staff from the municipality. Otherwise full bins could overflow.
33923.m: The municipality empties the public litter bins.

33924.e: People who have died are buried in the cemetery. Their relatives visit the graves there.
33924.m: The cemetery holds the graves of people who have died.

33925.q: How do you behave in a cemetery?
33925.e: In the cemetery, people mourn their loved ones who have died. That is why you are quiet and respectful there.
33925.m: In the cemetery, I am quiet and respectful.

33926.q: What often stands on a grave with the name of the person who died?
33926.e: The gravestone shows the name and often the dates of birth and death of the person who died.
33926.m: The gravestone shows the name of the person who died.

33927.q: What do relatives often bring to a grave?
33927.e: Many people bring flowers or light a candle. That shows that they are thinking of the person who died.
33927.m: Flowers on a grave show that you remember the person who died.

33928.q: Who is usually responsible for the cemetery in Switzerland?
33928.e: In Switzerland, the municipalities are usually responsible for cemeteries. They look after the paths and manage the graves.
33928.m: The municipality usually looks after the cemetery.

33929.q: What is a grave called in which many people rest together without their own gravestone?
33929.e: In a communal grave, many people who have died rest together. Their names are often on a shared plaque.
33929.m: In a communal grave, many people rest together.

a: A bell in the church tower
33930.e: After a cremation, the ashes are put into an urn. It can be buried in the cemetery.
33930.m: The ashes of a person who has died are kept in an urn.

33931.q: Who looks after the paths, trees and hedges in the cemetery?
33931.e: Cemetery gardeners keep the cemetery well cared for. They cut the hedges and look after the paths.
33931.m: The cemetery gardener looks after the cemetery.

33933.q: Who makes sure nobody drowns at the swimming pool?
33933.e: The lifeguard watches the water. In an emergency, they rescue people and give first aid.
33933.m: The lifeguard keeps an eye on everyone at the pool.

33934.q: What do you do before swimming at the swimming pool?
33934.e: Before swimming, you have a shower. That keeps the water in the pool cleaner.
33934.m: Before swimming, I have a shower.

33935.q: Why mustn't you run at the edge of the pool?
33935.e: The floor at the edge of the pool is wet and slippery. If you run, you can fall and hurt yourself.
33935.m: At the edge of the pool, I walk slowly.

33936.q: What is a swimming pool under a roof called, which is also open in winter?
33936.e: An indoor pool is inside a building. That is why you can swim there all year round.
33936.m: At the indoor pool, you can swim in winter too.

33937.e: In the non-swimmers' pool, the water is not deep. Children can stand and play there safely.
33937.m: In the non-swimmers' pool, you can stand in the water.

33938.q: What helps children at the swimming pool who can't swim well yet?
33938.e: Armbands help with practising, but they do not replace supervision. Children who can't swim always need an adult nearby.
33938.m: Children in the water always need supervision.

33939.q: What do many children learn at school or on a course at the swimming pool?
33939.e: In swimming lessons, children learn to swim and how to stay safe in the water. Many municipalities make the pool available for this.
33939.m: Learning to swim is important for safety.

33940.q: What does the municipality need taxes for?
33940.e: With taxes, the municipality pays for many tasks, for example schools, roads and the fire brigade. This benefits everyone.
33940.m: With taxes, the municipality pays for things for everyone.

33941.q: Who pays municipal taxes in Switzerland?
33941.e: Taxes are paid mainly by adults who earn money or have savings and property. Companies pay taxes too.
33941.m: Adults and companies pay taxes to the municipality.

33942.q: To which three levels do people in Switzerland pay taxes?
33942.e: In Switzerland there are taxes for the Confederation, the canton and the municipality. Each level uses them to pay for its own tasks.
33942.m: Taxes go to the Confederation, the canton and the municipality.

33943.q: What do you get every year to declare your taxes?
33943.e: In the tax return, you write down how much you earn and own. This is used to work out how much tax you pay.
33943.m: In the tax return, you declare your income.

33944.e: People who earn more money pay more tax. People who earn little pay less.
33944.m: Whoever earns more pays more tax.

33945.q: Who decides how high the municipal tax is in many municipalities?
33945.e: The tax rate is often decided by the voters at the municipal assembly or by the municipal parliament. That way the residents have a say.
33945.m: The voters have a say in the municipal tax.

33946.q: Is the municipal tax the same in all Swiss municipalities?
33946.e: Every municipality sets its own tax rate. That is why you pay more or less tax depending on where you live.
33946.m: Every municipality has its own tax level.

33948.q: Which vehicle pushes the snow off the road in winter?
33948.e: The snowplough has a wide blade at the front. It uses it to push the snow to the side.
33948.m: The snowplough clears snow from the road.

33949.q: What does the winter road service spread on icy roads?
33949.e: Salt makes the ice melt. Grit is small stones that stop you slipping.
33949.m: Salt and grit make roads safer in winter.

33950.q: When does the winter road service often start work when it snows?
33950.e: The winter road service often starts during the night or very early in the morning. That way the roads are clear when people go to work and school.
33950.m: The winter road service often clears the roads early in the morning.

33951.q: Where is black ice especially dangerous?
33951.e: On black ice, you can slip easily. That is why the winter road service makes roads and pavements safe.
33951.m: On black ice, I walk especially carefully.

33952.q: Why are snow poles put up at the side of the road in winter?
a: So that you can see the edge
So that birds can sit on them
So that children can climb them
33952.e: When there is a lot of snow, you can no longer see the edge of the road. The poles show the snowplough where the road ends.
33952.m: Snow poles show where the road ends.

33953.q: Which vehicle often clears the snow on narrow pavements?
a: A tractor with a field plough
33953.e: Pavements and cycle paths need narrow clearing vehicles. Big snowploughs are too wide for them.
33953.m: Small clearing vehicles clear narrow pavements.

33954.q: What should cars do when a snowplough is coming?
a: Stop in the middle of the road
33954.e: A snowplough drives slowly and throws snow to the side. That is why you keep your distance and don't overtake dangerously.
33954.m: Behind the snowplough, I keep my distance.

33955.q: Who is responsible for winter road clearing on municipal roads in many municipalities?
33955.e: The municipal works department clears the municipal roads. Bigger roads are often cleared by the canton.
33955.m: In winter, the works department clears the municipal roads.

33956.q: What is the municipal building called in many cities?
33956.e: In cities, the administration building is often called the city hall (Stadthaus). Many of the city's employees work there.
33956.m: In many cities, the municipal building is called the city hall.

33957.q: Many old towns have a beautiful old building where the council used to meet. What is it called?
33957.e: In the town hall, the town council used to meet. Many town halls are still in use today.
33957.m: The town council used to meet in the town hall.

33958.q: When is the municipal administration usually open?
33958.e: The counters at the municipal offices are usually open from Monday to Friday. At the weekend they are mostly closed.
33958.m: The municipal administration is usually open on weekdays.

33959.q: Where are important notices for everyone often put up at the municipal offices?
33959.e: The municipality puts up official notices on the notice board at the municipal offices. That way everyone can read them.
33959.m: You can read important notices on the notice board at the municipal offices.

33960.q: Who meets regularly at the municipal offices?
33960.e: The municipality's government usually holds its meetings at the municipal offices. There it discusses the municipality's tasks.
33960.m: The municipal council often holds its meetings at the municipal offices.

33961.q: What can you apply for at the counter of the municipal offices in many municipalities?
33961.e: In many cantons, you apply for an identity card at the municipality where you live. You get a driving licence from the canton's road traffic office.
33961.m: In many municipalities, you can apply for an identity card at the municipal offices.

33962.q: Who works at the counter in the municipal offices?
33962.e: Employees of the municipal administration work at the counter. They help residents with their questions.
33962.m: Municipal employees work in the municipal offices.

33963.q: Where do dog owners in many municipalities collect their dog tag?
33963.e: Dogs must be registered with the municipality. You pay the dog tax and in many municipalities you get a dog tag.
33963.m: In many municipalities, you get a dog tag from the municipal administration.

33964.q: Who elects the mayor of a municipality?
33964.e: The mayor (Gemeindepräsidentin) is elected by the voters of the municipality. These are adults with the right to vote who live there.
33964.m: The voters elect the mayor of the municipality.

33965.q: Who stands in for the mayor of the municipality when he is on holiday?
33965.e: Every municipality has someone who stands in for the mayor. This person is called the deputy or vice-president.
33965.m: The deputy stands in for the mayor.

33966.q: What is the head of a municipality called in Italian in the canton of Ticino?
33966.e: In Ticino, the person at the head of the municipality is called the “sindaco”. A woman in this office is called the “sindaca”.
33966.m: In Ticino, the head of the municipality is called the Sindaco.

33967.q: What is the head of a municipality called in French in the canton of Vaud?
33967.e: In Vaud and Fribourg, the head of the municipality is called the “syndic”. A woman in this office is called the “syndique”.
33967.m: In the canton of Vaud, the head of the municipality is called the Syndic.

33968.q: What does the mayor often do at the 1 August celebration in the village?
33968.e: At the National Day celebration, the mayor or a guest often speaks to the people. Speeches like this are part of many village festivals.
33968.m: At the 1 August celebration, the mayor often gives a speech.

33969.q: For how many years is the head of a municipality usually elected?
33969.e: In most cantons, a term of office in the municipality lasts four years. After that you can be re-elected.
33969.m: The head of a municipality is usually elected for four years.

33970.q: Who may become the head of a municipality in Switzerland?
33970.e: In Switzerland, women and men can be elected to the municipal government. Today, many women lead a municipality.
33970.m: Women and men may lead a municipality.

33971.q: In small municipalities, being mayor is often a part-time office. What does that mean?
a: You live in the municipal offices
You are never in the village
33971.e: In small municipalities, the mayor only works a few hours a week for the municipality. Besides that, they usually have another job.
33971.m: With a part-time office, you also have another job.

33972.q: How many people usually belong to the municipal council in a village?
33972.e: A municipal council usually has between three and nine members. Together they form the municipality's government.
33972.m: A municipal council usually has three to nine members.

33973.q: Why does a municipal council often have an odd number of members, for example 5?
a: So that there is no tie
So that everyone fits in the car
33973.e: With an odd number, there cannot be the same number of yes and no votes if everyone votes. So there is always a majority.
33973.m: An odd number of members prevents a tie.

33974.q: What do you call the area of responsibility of a municipal council member, for example schools or building?
33974.e: Each member of the municipal council is responsible for a portfolio. A portfolio can be, for example, finance, building or schools.
33974.m: Each municipal council member looks after their own portfolio.

33975.q: Who gives permission for someone to build a new house in many municipalities?
33975.e: Anyone who wants to build a house needs permission. This is called planning permission. In many municipalities, the municipal council decides on it.
33975.m: In many municipalities, the municipal council gives permission to build a house.

33976.q: Can you usually just go and watch when a village's municipal council has a meeting?
a: No, the meetings are usually not public
Yes, the meeting is shown on TV
33976.e: The meetings of the municipal government are usually not public. The municipal council informs the people about its decisions afterwards.
33976.m: The municipal council's meetings are usually not public.

33977.q: What does the municipal council prepare for the municipal assembly?
a: The proposals and items of business
33977.e: The municipal council prepares the business and makes proposals. At the municipal assembly, the voters then decide.
33977.m: The municipal council prepares the business for the municipal assembly.

33978.q: What is the municipal government called in French in the canton of Vaud?
33978.e: In Vaud, a municipality's government is called the “Municipalité”. It is led by the Syndic.
33978.m: In the canton of Vaud, the municipal government is called the Municipalité.

33979.q: Where do you usually have to live if you want to be elected to the municipal council?
33979.e: Members of the municipal council usually have to live in the municipality. After all, they represent the people who live there.
33979.m: Municipal council members usually live in their municipality.

33980.q: Who writes down at the municipal council meetings what was decided?
33980.e: The municipal clerk records what was discussed and decided. This document is called the minutes.
33980.m: The municipal clerk writes down what the municipal council decides.

33981.q: What does the municipal clerk often lead?
33981.e: In many municipalities, the municipal clerk is in charge of the administration staff. She is something like the head of the administration.
33981.m: The municipal clerk often leads the municipal administration.

33982.q: What is the municipal clerk called in a town?
33982.e: In a town, this office is called town clerk. The tasks are similar to those in a village.
33982.m: In a town, the municipal clerk is called the town clerk.

33983.q: Who employs the municipal clerk in many municipalities?
33983.e: Today the municipal clerk is usually employed by the municipal council. They work closely with the municipal council.
33983.m: The municipal council usually employs the municipal clerk.

33984.q: May the municipal clerk vote in the municipal council?
33984.e: The municipal clerk takes part in the meetings and gives advice. But only the elected members of the municipal council may vote.
33984.m: The municipal clerk advises the municipal council but does not vote.

33985.q: Who often signs important letters from the municipality together with the mayor?
33985.e: Important municipal documents often have two signatures. Alongside the mayor, the municipal clerk usually signs.
33985.m: Important municipal letters are often also signed by the municipal clerk.

33986.q: Where does the municipality keep old, important papers?
33986.e: Important old papers of the municipality are kept safely in the municipal archive. The municipal clerk is often responsible for it.
33986.m: The municipality keeps old, important papers in the municipal archive.

33987.q: Where does the municipal clerk have her office?
33987.e: The municipal clerk works for the administration. It has its offices in the municipal building.
33987.m: The municipal clerk works in the municipal offices.

33988.q: Where do you register when you move to a new municipality?
33988.e: Anyone who moves to a municipality must register at the residents' registration office. That way the municipality knows who lives there.
33988.m: After moving, you register at the residents' registration office.

33989.q: Within how many days do you usually have to register after moving house?
33989.e: In most cantons, you have to register with the new municipality within 14 days. That is two weeks.
33989.m: After moving, you usually register within 14 days.

33990.q: What must you do at your old municipality when you move away?
a: Write a letter to the Federal Council
33990.e: If you move away, you deregister at the residents' registration office of the old municipality. Then you register in the new municipality.
33990.m: When you move away, you deregister at the old municipality.

33991.q: What does the residents' registration office keep a record of?
a: Everyone who lives in the village
33991.e: The residents' registration office keeps the register of residents. It lists everyone who lives in the municipality.
33991.m: The residents' registration office keeps a list of all residents.

33992.q: What must you tell the residents' registration office if you move to another flat in the same village?
a: The colour of the new walls
33992.e: Even when moving within the municipality, the residents' registration office must know the new address. That way the register of residents stays correct.
33992.m: When moving within the same village, you report the new address.

33993.q: Which document do you get from the residents' registration office as proof of where you live?
33993.e: The residents' registration office can confirm that someone lives in the municipality. This document is called a certificate of residence.
33993.m: A certificate of residence shows where you live.

33994.q: What else is the residents' registration office called in some municipalities?
33994.e: Depending on the municipality, the office is called residents' registration office, residents' office or residents' services. The task is similar everywhere.
33994.m: The residents' registration office is sometimes called the residents' office.

33995.q: A family moves to a new village. Who must be registered?
a: Everyone in the family, including children
33995.e: Everyone who moves in is registered at the residents' registration office. Babies and children are included too.
33995.m: When moving house, the whole family is registered.

33996.q: Which flowers can be seen on the coat of arms of the town of Rapperswil-Jona?
33996.e: The coat of arms of Rapperswil-Jona shows the Rapperswil roses and a blue wavy line. That is why Rapperswil is also called the Town of Roses.
33996.m: The coat of arms of Rapperswil-Jona has roses on it.

33997.q: What is the knowledge of how coats of arms are designed and described called?
33997.e: Heraldry deals with coats of arms, their colours and pictures.
33997.m: The study of coats of arms is called heraldry.

33998.q: From which period do coats of arms originally come?
a: From the time of the dinosaurs
33998.e: The first coats of arms appeared about 900 years ago in the Middle Ages. Later, towns and villages also adopted such symbols.
33998.m: Coats of arms have existed since the Middle Ages.

33999.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of the city of St Gallen?
33999.e: The coat of arms of the city of St Gallen shows an upright bear with a golden collar. Emperor Frederick III allowed the collar in 1475.
33999.m: The city of St Gallen has a bear with a golden collar on its coat of arms.

34000.q: What does the coat of arms of the town of Biel show?
34000.e: The coat of arms of Biel/Bienne shows two silver crossed axes on a red background.
34000.m: The coat of arms of Biel has two crossed axes.

34001.q: Which animal stands in a town gate on the coat of arms of the town of Chur?
34001.e: The coat of arms of Chur shows a black, upright ibex in a red town gate on a silver background.
34001.m: On the coat of arms of Chur, an ibex stands in a town gate.

34002.q: Which animals are shown on the coat of arms of the town of Winterthur?
34002.e: The coat of arms of Winterthur is silver with a red diagonal band. Beside it walk two red lions.
34002.m: The coat of arms of Winterthur has two red lions.

34004.q: From how many inhabitants is a municipality in Switzerland often considered a town?
34004.e: A well-known rule of thumb in Switzerland is: a municipality with 10,000 or more inhabitants counts as a town. But some old places are also called towns with fewer inhabitants.
34004.m: A municipality often counts as a town from 10,000 inhabitants.

34005.q: What is the old part of a town with many historic buildings and narrow lanes called?
34005.e: The old town is the oldest part of a town. In Bern, the old town is even a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
34005.m: The oldest part of a town is called the old town.

34006.q: What did many towns have all around them in the past?
34006.e: In the past, towns protected themselves with high walls and gates. You can still see remains of them in many old towns today.
34006.m: In the past, many towns had a town wall.

34007.q: Where did farmers sell their vegetables and eggs in town in the past?
34007.e: Traders and farmers met in the market square. People from the town bought their food there.
34007.m: In the past, people bought food at the market in town.

34008.q: Which building stands in the middle of many old villages?
34008.e: Many villages grew up around a church. That is why its tower can often be seen from far away.
34008.m: In many villages, the church stands in the middle.

34009.q: What do you call a very small settlement with just a few houses?
34009.e: A hamlet consists of only a few houses or farms. It is smaller than a village and belongs to a municipality.
34009.m: A hamlet is a very small settlement with few houses.

34011.q: What do you call the municipalities located right around a big city?
34011.e: Around big cities like Zurich or Geneva there are many suburbs. Many people live there and work in the city.
34011.m: The municipalities around a big city are called suburbs.

34012.q: What does a big city usually have that a small village doesn't?
34012.e: Big Swiss cities like Zurich, Bern, Basel or Geneva have a tram network. Small villages have a bus at most.
34012.m: Trams usually run in big cities.

34013.q: What is the person who leads a town in Switzerland called?
34013.e: A town is led by the town president, similar to a mayor. In everyday Swiss German, people often say “Stapi”.
34013.m: The town president is at the head of a town.

34014.q: Which government does the town president of Zurich lead?
34014.e: In the city of Zurich, the government is called the city council (Stadtrat). The town president chairs its meetings.
34014.m: Zurich's town president leads the city council.

34015.q: How many members does the city government of Zurich have?
34015.e: Zurich's city council has nine members. Each one heads a department of the city.
34015.m: The city government of Zurich has nine members.

34016.q: What was special about the election of Corine Mauch in 2009?
a: She became Zurich's first female town president
She became the youngest Federal Councillor
She became the first woman in the National Council
She became President of the Confederation
34016.e: In 2009, Corine Mauch became the first woman to be town president of Zurich. She stayed in office for many years.
34016.m: In 2009, Corine Mauch became Zurich's first female town president.

34017.q: What is the government of the city of Bern called?
34017.e: In the city of Bern, the government is called the Municipal Council (Gemeinderat). The city parliament, on the other hand, is called the City Council (Stadtrat). Since 2025, Marieke Kruit has led the Municipal Council.
34017.m: In Bern, the city government is called the Municipal Council.

34018.q: How often does the office of Maire, the head of the city, change in Geneva?
34018.e: In Geneva, a different member of the city government takes on the office of Maire every year. That way everyone gets a turn.
34018.m: In Geneva, the office of Maire changes every year.

34019.q: What is the person at the head of a town in Germany called in German?
34019.e: In Germany and Austria, the head of a town is called the Bürgermeister, meaning mayor. In German-speaking Switzerland, people usually say Stadtpräsident.
34019.m: In German towns, the head of the town is called the Bürgermeister.

34020.q: How many members does the city government of Bern have?
34020.e: In the city of Bern, the government is called the Municipal Council and has five members. The head of the city is one of them and leads it.
34020.m: The city government of Bern has five members.

34021.q: Why does a big city usually have a parliament instead of a municipal assembly?
34021.e: In a big city, not all the voters would fit in one hall. That is why they elect representatives to the parliament.
34021.m: Big cities have a parliament because too many people live there.

34022.q: What is the city parliament of Zurich called?
34022.e: In Zurich, the city's parliament is called the Municipal Council (Gemeinderat). This can be confusing, because in villages the municipal council is the government.
34022.m: Zurich's city parliament is called the Municipal Council.

34023.q: What does the city parliament of Zurich do?
a: It decides the city's rules and budget
It leads the police on operations
34023.e: The city parliament decides rules for the city and the budget. The city government then puts these decisions into practice.
34023.m: The city parliament decides the city's rules and budget.

34024.q: What is the city parliament of Bern called?
34024.e: In Bern, the city's parliament is called the City Council (Stadtrat). In Zurich, on the other hand, the City Council is the government.
34024.m: Bern's city parliament is called the City Council.

34025.q: Who elects the members of the city parliament of Bern?
a: The voters of the city of Bern
34025.e: The voters of the city of Bern elect the members of their city parliament. In Bern, this parliament is called the City Council.
34025.m: The people of the city elect the city parliament.

34026.q: What is the municipal parliament called in some cantons, for example Aargau?
34026.e: In Aargau, Lucerne and Basel-Landschaft, a municipality's parliament is often called the Residents' Council (Einwohnerrat).
34026.m: In some cantons, the municipal parliament is called the Residents' Council.

34027.q: How often is the city parliament of Zurich elected?
34027.e: The members of Zurich's Municipal Council are elected by the people every four years. The election takes place together with the election of the city government.
34027.m: Zurich's city parliament is elected every four years.

34028.q: Who chairs the meetings of a city parliament?
34028.e: The parliament elects a president of the council from among its members. This office usually changes every year.
34028.m: The president of the council chairs the parliament's meetings.

34029.q: Do most Swiss municipalities have their own parliament?
a: No, most have a municipal assembly
No, they have nothing at all
34029.e: Only about one in five municipalities has a parliament (as of 2023), mainly towns and larger municipalities. In most others, the municipal assembly decides.
34029.m: Most Swiss municipalities have no parliament, but a municipal assembly.

34030.q: What is a municipal works depot?
a: A municipal service for roads and facilities
34030.e: The works depot holds the municipality's vehicles, tools and materials. From there, the staff look after roads, squares and facilities.
34030.m: The works depot looks after the municipality's roads and facilities.

34031.q: What does the works depot store in large amounts before winter?
34031.e: To fight black ice, the municipality needs a lot of road salt in winter. The works depot stores it in silos or sheds.
34031.m: In winter, the works depot stores road salt against black ice.

34032.q: What do the works depot staff often do on paths and squares in autumn?
34032.e: In autumn, lots of leaves fall on paths and squares. The works depot staff sweep them up so that nobody slips.
34032.m: In autumn, the works depot sweeps up the leaves.

34033.q: What do the works depot staff often do in parks in summer?
34033.e: In summer, the works depot looks after parks and green spaces. This includes mowing the grass and cutting hedges.
34033.m: In summer, the works depot mows the grass in the parks.

34034.q: Who mends a hole in a municipal road in many municipalities?
34034.e: The municipality is responsible for municipal roads. Small damage such as holes is mended by the works depot staff.
34034.m: The works depot mends holes in municipal roads.

34035.q: What does the works depot often bring for a village festival?
34035.e: For events, the works depot often provides festival benches, tables and crowd barriers. Afterwards it clears them away again.
34035.m: For village festivals, the works depot often provides tables and benches.

34036.q: Who repairs a broken park bench in many municipalities?
34036.e: Park benches, fountains and play equipment often belong to the municipality. The works depot staff repair them when something is broken.
34036.m: Broken park benches are often repaired by the works depot.

34037.q: Why do works depot staff often wear orange clothes on the road?
a: So that they can be seen easily
34037.e: Orange is a signal colour and really stands out. That way drivers see the workers on the road in good time.
34037.m: Orange clothes make sure workers on the road can be seen easily.

34038.q: What does the caretaker often use to clean the large floors in the school?
34038.e: For large areas such as corridors and gyms, the caretaker needs a cleaning machine. It scrubs and dries the floor in one go.
34038.m: The caretaker often cleans large floors with a machine.

34040.q: Who often locks up the school building in the evening?
34040.e: The caretaker has the keys to the school building. They often lock it in the evening and open it in the morning.
34040.m: The caretaker often locks up the school building.

34041.q: A light is flickering in the classroom. Who do you report it to?
34041.e: The caretaker is responsible for repairs in the school building. The teacher reports to them what is broken.
34041.m: You report broken things in the school to the caretaker.

34042.q: Who often makes sure in winter that the path to the school is clear of snow?
34042.e: The caretaker often clears the snow around the school building. That way the children can get into school safely.
34042.m: In winter, the caretaker often clears the snow at the school.

34043.q: Who often looks after the heating in the school building?
34043.e: The caretaker checks the heating and other systems in the building. That way the rooms are warm in winter.
34043.m: The caretaker often looks after the heating in the school.

34044.q: What does the caretaker often do in the school building during the summer holidays?
34044.e: When there are no children, the caretaker cleans the school building thoroughly. The floors and windows are cleaned then too.
34044.m: In the summer holidays, the caretaker cleans the school thoroughly.

34045.q: Where do forgotten jackets and PE bags often end up in the school?
34045.e: The caretaker often collects things that have been left behind in one place. You can pick them up again from there.
34045.m: The caretaker often collects things forgotten at school.

34046.q: What does the caretaker check so that everyone can get out of the school quickly in an emergency?
a: That the emergency exits are clear
34046.e: Emergency exits must never be blocked. In a fire, everyone must be able to get out quickly and safely.
34046.m: The caretaker makes sure the emergency exits are clear.

34047.q: What is in a municipal newsletter?
34047.e: The municipal newsletter reports on what is happening in the place. You find out, for example, about new projects and events.
34047.m: The municipal newsletter has news from the municipality.

34048.e: The municipal newsletter is published by the municipality itself. It informs the people who live there.
34048.m: The municipality publishes the municipal newsletter.

34049.q: How does the municipal newsletter usually reach people?
a: You have to buy it in a shop
You have to collect it from the municipal offices
Only if you order and pay for it
34049.e: Many municipalities deliver their newsletter free of charge to every household. That way it reaches all the residents.
34049.m: The municipal newsletter usually arrives free through the letterbox.

34050.q: What is often officially published in the municipal newsletter so that neighbours know about it?
34050.e: Anyone who wants to build has to make the planning application public. That way neighbours can see it and object if necessary.
34050.m: Planning applications are often published in the municipal newsletter.

34051.q: What else is the municipal newsletter called in some municipalities?
34051.e: Many municipalities call their newsletter a bulletin or municipal sheet. The content is similar.
34051.m: The municipal newsletter is sometimes called a bulletin.

34052.q: Who often announces their own events such as concerts or tournaments in the municipal newsletter?
34052.e: In many municipal newsletters, clubs may announce their events. That way everyone in the village hears about them.
34052.m: Clubs often announce their events in the municipal newsletter.

34053.q: Where else can you often find municipal news today?
34053.e: Many municipalities also put their news on the internet. Some even have their own app.
34053.m: Today you can often find municipal news on the municipality's website too.

34054.q: Who do many municipal newsletters publicly congratulate?
34054.e: Many municipal newsletters carry congratulations for older residents, for example on their 90th birthday.
34054.m: Many municipal newsletters congratulate residents on big birthdays.

34055.q: What does the municipal council often announce in the municipal newsletter?
34055.e: Because the meetings are not public, the municipal council informs people about its decisions in the newsletter.
34055.m: The municipal council reports its decisions in the municipal newsletter.

34056.q: What can the municipal assembly decide on, for example?
34056.e: At the municipal assembly, the voters decide on municipal matters. These include big buildings such as a new school.
34056.m: The municipal assembly decides on municipal matters.

34057.q: From what age may you vote at the municipal assembly in most municipalities?
34057.e: In Switzerland, you can usually vote from the age of 18. At 18 you are an adult.
34057.m: In Switzerland, you can usually vote from 18.

34058.q: How many times a year is there a municipal assembly in many municipalities?
34058.e: Many municipalities hold an assembly about twice a year. That way everyone can regularly have a say.
34058.m: Many municipalities hold a municipal assembly about twice a year.

34059.q: Where does a municipal assembly often take place?
34059.e: Many municipalities don't have a large hall. That is why people often meet in the gym or the multi-purpose hall.
34059.m: The municipal assembly often takes place in the gym.

34060.q: At what time of day is the municipal assembly usually held?
a: In the middle of the night
34060.e: Many adults work during the day. That is why the municipal assembly is usually in the evening.
34060.m: The municipal assembly is usually in the evening.

34061.q: How many voters usually come to a municipal assembly?
34061.e: All voters may come, but usually only a small share of them turn up. Those who come decide for the whole municipality.
34061.m: Usually only a small share of the voters come to the municipal assembly.

34062.q: Can you vote by post at a municipal assembly?
a: No, you have to be there
Yes, the neighbour votes for you
34062.e: At the municipal assembly, only people who are in the hall in person count. There are no postal votes there.
34062.m: At the municipal assembly, you have to be there yourself to vote.

34063.q: Who usually chairs the municipal assembly?
34063.e: The assembly is usually chaired by the mayor of the municipality. They call up the topics and lead the votes.
34063.m: The municipal assembly is usually chaired by the mayor.

34064.q: What can the voters do with a proposal from the municipal council?
34064.e: The municipal council makes proposals, but the assembly decides. It can accept or reject a proposal.
34064.m: The assembly can accept or reject a proposal.

34065.q: Where do guests sit at the municipal assembly who are not allowed to vote?
34065.e: Guests may watch but not vote. That is why they sit separately, so that no wrong hands are counted.
34065.m: Guests at the municipal assembly sit in their own seats.

34066.q: Who may put forward their own motion at the municipal assembly?
34066.e: At the municipal assembly, every person entitled to vote may put forward a motion. The assembly then votes on it.
34066.m: All voters may put forward motions at the assembly.

34067.q: For yes, 52 people raise their hands, for no, 38. How many more hands does yes have?
34067.e: You work out 52 − 38 = 14. So yes has 14 more hands than no.
34067.m: You find the difference with a subtraction.

34068.q: May you raise your hand at the municipal assembly for a friend who is ill?
34068.e: At the municipal assembly, each person votes only for themselves. Anyone who is not there cannot vote.
34068.m: At the municipal assembly, you only vote for yourself.

34069.q: What do voters in some municipalities hold up when voting?
34069.e: Some municipalities hand out voting cards to voters at the entrance. When voting, you hold up the card, so it is clear who may vote.
34069.m: In some municipalities, you hold up a voting card when voting.

34070.q: How long do you keep your hand up when voting?
a: Until the votes have been counted
34070.e: The vote counters need time to count all the hands. That is why you keep your hand up until they have finished.
34070.m: You keep your hand up until the counting is done.

34071.q: What may you do at the municipal assembly before a vote?
34071.e: Before the vote, you can ask to speak. That way everyone hears the arguments for and against something.
34071.m: Before the vote, you may give your opinion.

34072.q: The vote counters count 12 raised hands in each of three rows. How many hands is that altogether?
34072.e: You work out 3 times 12 = 36. So there are 36 hands altogether.
34072.m: You can quickly count groups of the same size with a multiplication.

34073.q: When are the vote counters especially important?
34073.e: When almost the same number say yes and no, you have to count exactly. Then every vote matters.
34073.m: When a result is close, you have to count exactly.

34074.q: What is the plan of how much money the municipality will spend next year called?
34074.e: In the budget, the municipality plans its income and spending for the next year. The voters have to approve it.
34074.m: In the budget, the municipality plans its money.

34075.q: Where does the municipality get most of its money from?
34075.e: The people and companies in the village pay taxes. The municipality uses this money to pay for its tasks.
34075.m: The municipality gets its money mainly from taxes.

34076.q: What is the statement called that shows how much money the municipality really spent last year?
34076.e: The budget is a plan, while the annual accounts show the real result. The annual accounts must also be approved by the voters.
34076.m: The annual accounts show how much money the municipality really spent.

34077.q: Who has to accept the budget at the municipal assembly?
34077.e: The municipal council makes a proposal for the budget. The voters then decide whether to accept it.

34078.q: When is the budget for the next year usually decided?
a: Towards the end of the year
34078.e: The budget is for the next year. That is why it is usually decided in November or December.
34078.m: The budget is usually decided towards the end of the year.

34079.q: What does the budget show if the municipality spends more than it takes in?
34079.e: When spending is greater than income, there is a minus. This is also called a deficit.
34079.m: If you spend more than you take in, there is a minus.

34080.q: In which currency does a Swiss municipality calculate its budget?
34080.e: In Switzerland, people pay with francs and centimes. The municipalities also calculate their money in francs.

34081.q: Who makes the first proposal for the municipality's budget?
34081.e: The municipal council is the municipality's government. It prepares the budget and presents it to the assembly.
34081.m: The municipal council makes the proposal for the budget.

34082.q: What do you call money that the municipality has borrowed and must pay back?
34082.e: When a municipality borrows money, for example for a new school, it has debts. It has to pay them back later.
34082.m: Borrowed money that has to be paid back is debt.

34083.q: Who often decides whether an expensive new playground is built?
34083.e: A new playground costs a lot of money. That is why the voters at the municipal assembly often decide on it.
34083.m: The municipal assembly often decides on an expensive playground.

34084.q: What does the municipality need to build a playground?
34084.e: A playground needs a piece of land and money for equipment. The municipality has to plan both.
34084.m: A playground needs money and space.

34085.q: What is the money called that the assembly approves for a particular project?
34085.e: For a project such as a playground, the assembly must approve a credit. Then the municipality may spend the money.
34085.m: For a project, the assembly approves a credit.

34086.q: How can children say what they would like on a new playground?
34086.e: Children may not vote. But they can send wishes and drawings to the municipality.
34086.m: Children can send their ideas to the municipality.

34087.q: What is especially important at a playground?
34087.e: Play equipment must be safe so that nobody gets hurt. That is why there are rules for play equipment and soft ground.

34088.q: What is often put under a swing so that falls are soft?
34088.e: Under play equipment there is often soft ground such as wood chips, sand or rubber mats. That way a fall hurts less.
34088.m: There is soft ground under play equipment.

34089.q: Where is the best place for a municipality to build a playground?
a: In the middle of a car park
34089.e: Children should be able to reach the playground easily on foot and play safely. That is why it is planned near homes and away from heavy traffic.
34089.m: A playground belongs near homes and away from traffic.

34090.q: What happens if the assembly says no to the playground?
34090.e: The municipality must stick to the assembly's decision. If the majority says no, the playground is not built.
34090.m: The municipality sticks to the assembly's decision.

34091.q: How do people find out that a municipal assembly is taking place?
a: Through an invitation from the municipality
Through a letter from the Federal Council
34091.e: The municipality sends out an invitation or announces it publicly. It gives the date, time and place.
34091.m: The municipality sends invitations to the assembly.

34092.q: What is the list of topics for the municipal assembly called?
34092.e: The agenda lists all the business that will be discussed at the assembly. A single topic is called an agenda item.
34092.m: The agenda lists the topics of the assembly.

34093.q: What is on the invitation to the municipal assembly?
34093.e: So that everyone can come, the invitation says when and where the assembly is. It also lists the topics.
34093.m: The invitation gives the date, time and place.

34094.q: Why do you get the invitation to the municipal assembly weeks in advance?
a: So that you have to register
So that you pay to get in
So that you reserve a seat
34094.e: You should have time to read the topics and think about them. That way you can vote well prepared.
34094.m: With the invitation, you can prepare.

34095.q: Where can you look at the documents for the municipal assembly beforehand?
34095.e: Before the assembly, the documents are available at the municipal administration. You can read them there in peace.
34095.m: You can look at the assembly documents at the municipal administration.

34096.q: Who gets the invitation to the municipal assembly?
a: All the children in the village
34096.e: Everyone who may vote in the municipality is invited. They usually receive the documents at home.
34096.m: The voters are invited to the assembly.

34097.q: What is a single topic on the agenda called?
34097.e: Each piece of business at the assembly is an agenda item. Several of them together make up the agenda.
34097.m: A single topic of the assembly is called an agenda item.

34098.q: Where can you often find the invitation to the assembly today as well?
34098.e: Many municipalities put the invitation and the documents on their website. That way you can read them at any time.
34098.m: The invitation is often also on the municipality's website.

34099.q: What is the place called that appears in a Swiss passport as the family's place of origin?
34099.e: Every Swiss citizen has a place of origin. It is written in their passport and identity card.
34099.m: The place of origin is written in the Swiss passport.

a: People with citizenship of the municipality
All the tourists in the village
34100.e: Local citizens have citizenship of this municipality. So the municipality is their place of origin.
34100.m: Local citizens have citizenship of their municipality.

34101.q: Do you have to live in your place of origin?
34101.e: Many people don't live in their place of origin at all. The place of origin shows where the family has its citizenship.
34101.m: You don't have to live in your place of origin.

34102.q: How does a child usually get their place of origin?
a: From the hospital where they were born
34102.e: A child usually gets their place of origin from their parents. That is why families often have the same place of origin.
34102.m: Children usually get their place of origin from their parents.

34103.q: What is the community of all local citizens of a municipality called?
34103.e: In many cantons, the local citizens form a citizens' community. It often owns woodland or land.
34103.m: The local citizens form a citizens' community.

34104.q: What does a citizens' community often own?
34104.e: Many citizens' communities own woodland, meadows or buildings. They look after this property.

34105.q: What is it called when someone from abroad becomes Swiss?
34105.e: With naturalisation, a person receives Swiss citizenship. This also includes citizenship of a municipality.
34105.m: Someone who becomes Swiss is naturalised.

34106.q: What is the minimum number of places of origin you have if you are Swiss?
34106.e: All Swiss citizens have at least one place of origin. Some have several.
34106.m: All Swiss citizens have at least one place of origin.

34107.q: What do you call people who have just moved to a municipality?
34107.e: Someone who has just moved to a municipality is a newcomer. Newcomers come from another place.
34107.m: Someone who has just moved to a village is a newcomer.

34108.q: What do you call people who move away from a municipality?
34108.e: Someone who leaves a municipality and lives elsewhere is moving away. The opposite is a newcomer.
34108.m: Someone who leaves is moving away.

34110.q: Who do you give your new address to after moving so that letters arrive correctly?
34110.e: The post office needs to know where to deliver the letters. You can tell it your new address, and then it forwards your letters.
34110.m: After moving, you tell the post office your new address.

34111.q: Which school do newcomers' children usually go to?
a: The school where they now live
34111.e: Children usually go to school where they live. After moving, they attend the school of the new municipality.
34111.m: Children go to school where they now live.

34112.q: How can newcomers quickly get to know new people in the village?
34112.e: In clubs you meet people with the same hobbies. That way newcomers quickly make contacts.
34112.m: In a club, you quickly get to know new people.

34113.q: When may adult Swiss newcomers vote in their new municipality?
a: As soon as they have registered
34113.e: Swiss voters may vote where they live. To do so, they must be registered there.
34113.m: Anyone who is registered may vote where they live.

34114.q: What do newcomers often bring to a village?
34114.e: New people bring experience from other places with them. That brings new ideas into village life.

34115.q: What is it called when two municipalities become one?
34115.e: In a municipal merger, two or more municipalities join together. After that there is only one municipality.
34115.m: In a municipal merger, municipalities become one.

34116.q: Who usually decides whether municipalities merge?
34116.e: The voters of the municipalities involved vote on a merger. So they have a say.
34116.m: The voters vote on a municipal merger.

34117.q: What happens to the number of municipalities after a merger?
34117.e: Several municipalities become one. So afterwards there are fewer municipalities.
34117.m: After a merger there are fewer municipalities.

34118.q: Which canton merged its many municipalities into just three in 2011?
34118.e: In the canton of Glarus, the 25 municipalities were merged into three in 2011. They are called Glarus, Glarus Nord and Glarus Süd.
34118.m: Since 2011 the canton of Glarus has had only three municipalities.

34119.q: What does a new municipality often get after a merger?
34119.e: After a merger the new municipality needs a name. Sometimes it gets a completely new one, sometimes it keeps an old one.
34119.m: A merged municipality often gets a new name.

34120.q: Why do small municipalities often merge?
a: To do their jobs better together
To get more seats in the National Council
So they no longer charge taxes
34120.e: Small municipalities sometimes find it hard to get people for the official posts. Together they can do their jobs better.
34120.m: Small municipalities merge to be stronger together.

34121.q: What still remains after a municipal merger?
34121.e: The houses and villages stay where they are. Only the administration is combined.
34121.m: After a merger the villages remain.

34122.q: On which day does a new, merged municipality usually begin?
34122.e: Municipal mergers usually take effect at the start of a year. That way the new municipality can start with its own budget.
34122.m: Merged municipalities usually start on 1 January.

34123.q: What is a gathering called where a municipality welcomes new residents?
34123.e: Many municipalities invite people who have just moved there to a newcomers' welcome event. There they are made to feel welcome.
34123.m: At the newcomers' welcome event the municipality greets new residents.

34124.q: Who is invited to a newcomers' welcome event?
a: People who have just moved there
34124.e: The people invited are those who have recently moved to the municipality. They can often bring their family.
34124.m: New residents are invited to the newcomers' welcome event.

34125.q: What do newcomers learn about at a newcomers' welcome event?
34125.e: The municipality introduces itself and shows what the village has to offer. That helps new people find their way around.
34125.m: At the newcomers' welcome event you get to know your new municipality.

34126.q: Who often greets the guests at a newcomers' welcome event?
34126.e: The mayor, who is the president of the municipality, often gives a short speech. That way the newcomers get to know the authorities.
34126.m: The mayor often speaks at the newcomers' welcome event.

34127.q: What is often served at the end of a newcomers' welcome event?
34127.e: After the speeches there is often something to drink and eat. During this apéro people can chat with each other.
34127.m: After the newcomers' welcome event there are often drinks and snacks.

34128.q: Who else often introduces themselves at a newcomers' welcome event?
34128.e: Clubs show what they do at the event. That way newcomers quickly find a hobby that suits them.
34128.m: The clubs often introduce themselves at the newcomers' welcome event.

34129.q: What is the aim of a newcomers' welcome event?
34129.e: New residents should feel at home in the village. So the municipality gives them a friendly welcome.
34129.m: The newcomers' welcome event welcomes new people.

34130.q: What do some municipalities do with the guests at a newcomers' welcome event?
34130.e: On a walk the newcomers are shown important places in the village. These include the school and the municipal offices, for example.
34130.m: A walk round the village shows newcomers the important places.

34131.q: What is the club called where people sing together?
34131.e: In a choir, lots of people sing songs together. Many villages have a church choir or a men's or women's choir.
34131.m: In a choir people sing together.

34132.q: In which village club do people play brass band music?
34132.e: The village band plays brass band music, for example at village festivals. Many villages have their own band.
34132.m: The village band plays brass band music.

34133.q: What is the club called where people do gymnastics together?
34133.e: In a gymnastics club people do sport and exercises together. Many gymnastics clubs have a group for children.
34133.m: In a gymnastics club people do gymnastics together.

34134.q: What is the person called who leads a club?
34134.e: The president leads the club. He or she chairs the meetings.

34135.q: Who looks after the money in a club?
34135.e: The treasurer manages the club's money. He or she writes down all the income and spending.
34135.m: The treasurer manages the money in a club.

34136.q: What do members usually pay to a club every year?
34136.e: With the membership fees the club pays for things like equipment or courses. They are usually paid once a year.

34137.q: What are the rules a club writes down called?
34137.e: Every club has statutes. They say, for example, what the club is for and how decisions are made.
34137.m: A club's rules are called its statutes.

34138.q: What is the meeting of all a club's members called?
34138.e: All the members meet at the general meeting. There they elect the committee, for example.
34138.m: All club members meet at the general meeting.

34139.q: Which village club helps with first aid when there are accidents?
34139.e: Samaritans learn first aid. They help out at festivals and sports events, for example.
34139.m: The Samaritan association helps with first aid.

34140.q: What is the festival called when decorated cows come down from the Alpine pasture to the village in autumn?
34140.e: In autumn the herders bring the cattle back from the Alpine pasture to the valley. The cows wear flowers and bells, and the village celebrates.
34140.m: At the Alpine descent the decorated cows come back from the Alpine pasture.

34141.q: Where is a village festival often held when it rains?
34141.e: For big festivals, clubs often put up a festival tent. Everyone stays dry inside, even when it rains.
34141.m: At a village festival you stay dry in the festival tent.

34142.q: What is a village fair with rides and market stalls in autumn often called?
34142.e: The Chilbi is a traditional fair with a merry-go-round, stalls and food. Many villages celebrate it once a year.
34142.m: The Chilbi is a village fair with rides and stalls.

34143.q: Who often helps so that a village festival can take place?
34143.e: Clubs set up stalls, cook and sell things. They often use the money to fill their club funds.
34143.m: Clubs often help with the village festival.

34144.q: What do people carry through the village in the turnip lantern parade?
34144.e: For the turnip lantern parade, children carve patterns into turnips. A light burns inside, and everyone walks through the village with them.
34144.m: In the turnip lantern parade you carry a glowing turnip.

34145.q: What is a village festival good for?
34145.e: At a village festival young and old come together. That way you get to know the people in the village better.
34145.m: At the village festival the people of the village meet.
